- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 3–8% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; increase forecast mid-period to reflect sentiment reversal.
- Model underperforms in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 3–5% upward bias to capture momentum.
- Model overestimates in late horizon (last 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply 3–5% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1, -1, 1” cycles, model exhibits lagged reaction; delay peak forecast by 1–3 days and reduce amplitude.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift; apply 1–3% mean-reversion correction toward recent 7-day average.
